text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 1: Quick-wins intervals cover more outcomes than production's'

g.text: Figure 1: Quick-wins intervals cover more outcomes than production's

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Corrected wind and radiation inputs; NGED solar and wind farms. Fold A: July 2025 to June 2026 Primary training settings (main). Coverage is the fraction of observed power readings inside a forecast interval. Both recipes predict power from 51 alternative weather forecasts. A quantile is a threshold below which a specified fraction of outcomes should fall. Production uses one power prediction for each; quick-wins pools nine quantiles for each: 459 values. The 80% band uses the 10th and 90th sample percentiles; the 90% band uses the 5th and 95th. Endpoints select the first sorted value whose cumulative fraction reaches the percentile. Dots average coverage equally across meters, then across three XGBoost training runs. All forecast horizons are included. Different seeds control each run's random choices. No uncertainty ranges were estimated for these coverage means. Dashed lines mark requested coverage, which finite, structured samples do not guarantee. If the samples and outcome are independent draws from one continuous distribution, expected coverage depends on sample size. Neither recipe's predictions are claimed to be independent draws from one distribution. Coverage alone cannot rank recipes; compare forecast loss and interval width too. All rows are exploratory.'
